author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
occasion: The work is a concise statement of Trinitarian faith. The source does not specify any occasion, addressee, or polemical target.
argument: Gregory declares that there is one God the Father, Father of the living Word and of the only-begotten Son. He then confesses one Lord, alone from the Father alone, God from God, the character and image of the Godhead, the active Word, the wisdom that contains the constitution of all things, and the power that creates the whole creation. He further confesses one Holy Spirit, who has existence from God and is manifested through the Son, that is, to human beings, the perfect image of the perfect Son, cause of life for the living, holy spring, and giver of holiness. The Trinity is perfect, undivided and unalienated in glory, eternity, and kingdom; nothing created, servile, or added later exists in it, and the Trinity remains always unchanging and unalterable.

outline.move: The whole work confesses the one God and Father, the one Lord as his true and eternal Son, and the one Holy Spirit, then affirms the perfect, undivided, unchanging Trinity.

cast.name: God the Father
cast.who: The one God, Father of the living Word, and Father of the only-begotten Son.

cast.name: The Lord, the Son
cast.who: The one Lord, only Son of the Father, God from God, image of the Godhead. The source never uses the name 'Jesus Christ'; the figure is referred to only as 'Lord' and 'Son.'

cast.name: Holy Spirit
cast.who: The one Holy Spirit, having existence from God and manifested through the Son, that is, to human beings.

voices.speaker: Gregory Thaumaturgus
voices.how_marked: The entire section is presented as the author's own confession.

key_terms.sense: The living Word, the Son, active in creation and revelation.
The exact impress or character of the Godhead, applied to the Son as the Father's perfect expression.
Image, used for the Son as image of the Godhead and the Spirit as image of the Son.
Wisdom, identified with the Son as the wisdom that contains and orders all things.
Power, identified with the Son as the creative power of the whole creation.
The Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, perfect and undivided.
Only-begotten, describing the unique sonship of the Son.
Eternal, applied to the Father, the Son, and the Trinity.
Unchanging and unalterable, describing the permanent identity of the Trinity.
Created thing, denied of anything within the Trinity.
Servant or slave, denied of anything within the Trinity.

scripture: No direct scriptural citations are given. The language echoes biblical titles for the Son and Spirit, especially from the Gospel of John and Pauline writings, but no book names or numbering conventions are used.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Father of the living Word and of the only-begotten Son
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Εἷς Θεὸς Πατὴρ Λόγου ζῶντος, σοφίας ὑφεστώσης καὶ δυνάμεως, καὶ χαρακτῆρος ἀϊδίου, τέλειος, τελείου γεννήτωρ· Πατὴρ Υἱοῦ μονογενοῦς
_unresolved_facts.fix: Father of the living Word, of subsistent wisdom and power and eternal character, perfect generator of the perfect; Father of the only-begotten Son. The 'living Word' and 'only-begotten Son' are the same person, not two separate objects of Fatherhood.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the wisdom that contains the constitution of all things
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: σοφία τῆς τῶν ὅλων συστάσεως περιεκτικὴ
_unresolved_facts.fix: wisdom comprehensive/containing of the constitution of all things

_unresolved_facts.claim: cause of life for the living
_unresolved_facts.fix: life, cause of the living / cause of life for the living (the Greek ζωὴ is 'life,' not 'cause of life'; ζώντων αἰτία is 'cause of the living'—the brief's rendering obscures the syntax)

_unresolved_facts.claim: The source never uses the name 'Jesus Christ'; the figure is referred to only as 'Lord' and 'Son.'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The figure is also referred to as 'Word' (Λόγος), not only 'Lord' and 'Son.'
